shortlist.admission: A family to investigate; arbitrary members and special points are not assumed nonalgebraic.
shortlist.method_exclusion: No full-rank maximal toric degeneration preserving this Weil structure; this is not an algebraicity obstruction.

shortlist.admission: Higher-dimensional reserve; cited genus-three semiregularity proof does not automatically extend.

discriminant_convention: det(h) in Q^*/Nm(K^*), without an extra (-1)^n normalization; split has class (-1)^n in complex dimension 2n.
norm_certificate: 3 is not a rational norm from Q(i): clearing denominators in a^2+b^2=3 and reduction modulo 3 forces all three primitive integer coordinates divisible by 3.
determinant_necessity: A half-dimensional K-isotropic subspace gives a Gram matrix [[0,B],[B*,C]], whose determinant is (-1)^n Nm(det B). Thus maximal degeneration requires the split discriminant; failure does not imply nonalgebraicity.
special_point_control: The diagonal period J=diag(i,i,i,-i,-i,-i) gives a product of elliptic curves in the nonsplit family; a nonsplit discriminant alone cannot imply nonalgebraicity.
next_action: Bind a marked member or rigorously constructed generic member and an independently specified Weil determinant class, retaining its reviewed status and all-cycle obstruction gates. No candidate is selected by this audit.
